# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I will establish a four-gesture code so the Mute can report the manual’s result to me: thumbs-up for YES, thumbs-down for NO, raised palm for HOLD, and OK for DONE. I will also tell the Blind to wait, since no action should occur before the code is established.

```text
speak(text="Gesture code: 👍 means YES, 👎 means NO, ✋ means HOLD, and 👌 means DONE. Blind, wait.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The Mute has sent 👍, which under the agreed code means YES. I am relaying that verdict to the Blind; no specific physical operation has been identified yet, so the Blind should hold.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute reports YES. HOLD; no physical operation has been identified yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The Mute reports HOLD. I will pass that instruction to the Blind and avoid suggesting any operation until the manual provides a more specific verdict.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute reports HOLD. Do not operate anything yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The repeated HOLD means the Mute’s manual has not authorized an operation yet. The Blind needs the bomb’s visible state, so I am transmitting the display, light, plate marking, and wire colors directly. I will continue waiting rather than guess at a wire or control.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state: display 0; light off; plate engraved question mark; wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. Mute still reports HOLD.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The Mute continues to report HOLD, so there is still no authorized action. I will keep the Blind from touching the bomb and wait for a changed manual verdict.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD continues. Do not touch or operate the bomb; wait for a changed verdict.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The Mute still signals HOLD, so the manual has not given permission for an operation. I will again instruct the Blind to keep the bomb untouched; guessing among the three wires would be unsafe.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD remains the manual verdict. Keep hands off the bomb and wait.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The repeated HOLD is not enough to identify a safe operation. The Blind must now inspect the bomb by touch and describe its controls to the Mute, without actuating anything. I am adding a compact numeric code so the Mute can relay which numbered control or wire the Blind reports.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New gesture code: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, and 🤟 means 3. When Blind reports tactile controls, relay the relevant number with these gestures; use ✋ for HOLD and 👌 for DONE.")
speak(to="blind", text="Feel the bomb carefully and describe every tactile control, socket, switch, button, or wire connection to Mute. Do not actuate anything. Mute, relay any numbered item using the new number gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The Mute still signals HOLD, and no tactile report from the Blind has reached me. I will ask the Blind to give the Mute a complete verbal inventory of the bomb’s tactile controls, explicitly separating observation from any operation. The Mute should continue using HOLD unless the manual gives a definite instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Please verbally report to Mute every tactile control and connection you can identify, including labels or positions, without activating anything. Mute, keep signaling HOLD until you have both the manual verdict and the Blind's report.")
wait()
```
